stem: A Network Load Balancer's target group has five targets in Availability Zone A and one target in Availability Zone B that keeps dropping packets under heavy traffic, and the dropped-packet target runs on an older instance family. Select TWO actions that address these two problems. (Select TWO.)

choices.text: Increase the Network Load Balancer's connection idle timeout
Enable cross-zone load balancing on the Network Load Balancer's target group
Reduce the Network Load Balancer to a single Availability Zone
Move the affected target to an instance family that supports enhanced networking
Change the target group's target type from instance to IP address

rationale: Cross-zone load balancing spreads requests evenly across targets in every enabled Availability Zone, which corrects the uneven five-to-one split. Moving the affected target to an instance family with enhanced networking raises the packet-per-second ceiling that was causing the dropped packets. Increasing the idle timeout changes how long an inactive connection stays open; it does not touch packet-per-second performance or the AZ imbalance. Reducing the load balancer to a single Availability Zone would remove the imbalance but also removes the multi-AZ resilience the deployment is meant to keep. Changing the target type from instance to IP address changes how targets are registered; it does not raise a target's packet-processing ceiling.
